articleTitle: Semi-anechoic chamber site attenuation calculations (EM waves)
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The reflectivity of an absorber-covered surface depends on the angle of incidence and the polarization as well as the frequency of the incident electromagnetic wave. The problem of calculating all of the angles involved in multiple reflection paths can be simplified by using the method of images. The author shows how the angles can be computed in a straightforward fashion using images. In addition he comments on the limitations of the absorber and image models in representing actual chambers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The GTEM cell concept; applications of this new EMC test environment to radiated emission and susceptibility measurements
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The use of a TEM-cell anechoic chamber hybrid, the GTEM cell for EMI testing, is discussed. The hybrid chamber may be used for both susceptibility and radiated emission testing and is well suited for time domain as well as continuous wave (CW) measurements. The chamber has extremely broadband characteristics, with a usable frequency range from DC to GHz ( approximately 18 GHz). The TEM mode is used to simulate an incident plane wave for susceptibility testing. Radiated emission data obtained in the hybrid chamber may be used to simulate open area test sites (OATS) or free space measurements. Applications will be stressed and a variety of representative data will be shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Remarks to the solution of EMC-problems on printed-circuit-boards
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author gives a survey of the PCB design process under EMC constraints. For a better understanding of the PCB design process with respect to EMC problems the standard design process is discussed first. Based on this discussion an alternate design process including EMC problems is defined. For this approach the PCB design problems are classified first. After this discussion the present state of the art and development of methods to handle noise phenomena on PCBs are worked out. New promising approaches are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Onboard aircraft measurements and techniques for whole aircraft EMC clearance
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Provides an overview of the state-of-the-art measurement techniques used to assess the electromagnetic compatibility between various systems onboard a modern aircraft. Avionic equipment susceptibility assessments and wiring loom induced current measurements are carried out using aircraft onboard transmitting systems. Bulk current injection techniques (BCI) are applied to the aircraft wiring looms to determine avionic equipment malfunction profiles in terms of frequency and amplitude. Safety margins can then be determined using the results of these measurements. Measurement techniques are described to assess the performance of antenna based systems including VSWR, antenna noise due to radiated emissions, antenna to antenna 'inband' coupling and harmonic frequency coupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Helmholtz coils for EMI immunity testing: stretching the uniform field area
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Helmholtz coils are used to establish known, uniform magnetic fields for calibrating magnetic field sensors, for EMI immunity testing, for magnetic bioeffects research, etc. But in the past, it has been assumed that only very small devices could be tested. The paper provides information leading to an understanding of the size of the uniform field region and how to trade off field uniformity for increased size of the device under test. Graphs and a table are provided to assist the helmholtz coil user in this task.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characterization of transient and CW disturbances induced in telephone subscriber lines
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: At the time the investigations started the authors knew that the EMC Working Group of the ZVEI in Germany had already made some progress with collecting data in their country. Therefore, it was decided to carry out at least the same measurements in the Netherlands. By doing so, there is the possibility of comparing the results obtained in both countries and adding to the collected data. These measurements as well as some additional ones are outlined. The measuring results are discussed, and where possible, the results are compared and combined with results obtained by the ZVEI.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new test-cell for the characterisation of shielding materials in the far field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: A TEM-cell with rectangular cross-section and used in the transmission-mode is described, with its basic characteristics. The points discussed include: advantages of this cell, compared with existing test methods for shielding materials; use of the test-cell for different materials (metals, coated textiles, coated plastics, conductive (filled) plastics) and the correlation with other techniques; use of the test-cell for small samples of shielding materials, using typical sample-holders and the effect of this; use of the test-cell for the characterisation for joints and gaskets; and modelling of the test-cell and the measuring-set-up.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A novel technique for damping site attenuation resonances in shielded semi-anechoic rooms
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Presents a simple and economical technique for suppressing resonance problems in shielded semi-anechoic rooms (SSARs). The work described is an application to an SSAR of a technique developed by Dawson and Marvin for small shielded enclosures. It consists of putting lossy dielectric blocks at well-selected positions where the electric fields of the problem-causing resonant modes show up a maximum. The chamber was designed primarily to perform EMI measurements at 3 m distance. However, it is also being used for irradiation measurements. Site attenuation measurements were performed in the 30-1000 MHz band to check the performance of the chamber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Undergraduate student projects on determining demodulation RFI statistics for operational amplifiers
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: A team of five undergraduate Electrical Engineering students under the supervision of a graduate student have measured RFI effects in an inverting operational amplifier (op amp) circuit with a voltage gain equal to ten for two sets of input and feedback resistor values. For the first case, the input resistor R1 is 10 k Omega , and the feedback resistor R2 is 100 k Omega . For the second case, R1 is 0.1 M Omega and R2 is 1 M Omega . Measurements were made with and without the RFI suppression capacitor C2=27 pF shunting R2. Each student was assigned 25 to 30 op amps of one type. The five op amp types tested and their input transistor type are the following: (1) 741 (bipolar NPN); (2) LM10 (bipolar PNP); (3) LF355 (JFET); (4) CA081 (MOSFET); (5) OP27 (NPN bipolar).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An equivalent circuit model for arbitrarily-shaped metallisation areas on printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author describes an equivalent circuit model which has been developed to predict the electrical behaviour of large or irregularly shaped areas of metallisation on printed circuit boards. An understanding of the behaviour of such areas can be vital in achieving successful implementation of RF circuit designs. The underlying theory for the model is described briefly, and steps taken to ensure the efficiency of the implementation are mentioned. The method of subdivision of these areas into a set of rectangular and triangular patches is detailed, and it is shown how these are associated with components in the equivalent circuit. Results are presented to show the accuracy which can be achieved with this model, and the usefulness of the results in gaining an understanding of the behaviour of these areas.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of an asymmetric TEM-cell for immunity testing
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: An asymmetric TEM-cell is analyzed in terms of field uniformity, bandwidth and characteristic impedance. Measured values are compared with calculated values. If optimally designed, an asymmetric TEM-cell is an attractive alternative to a symmetric TEM-cell.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Screening performances of triaxial cables with optimum braided shields
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author investigates the shielding effectiveness of triaxial cables employing optimum designs for braids in their inner and outer shields. This is done by calculating the time and frequency domain responses of inner-most line to the fields induced on the shield of the outer line. For most optimised braids, transfer admittance is in the same order of transfer impedance and thus both of these parameters were employed in the crosstalk model. Since the objective was to identify triaxial configurations which would yield minimum crosstalk, several designs including both standard and optimized braid constructions were simulated and studied numerically. Triaxial configurations with shorted intermediate circuit are used in all simulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Observation of electromagnetic coupling and power flow in printed circuits
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The performance of electronic equipment is determined by the distribution of electromagnetic power in the equipment. This depends on the location and electrical parameters of the sources of power and the physical configuration and material properties of the equipment. The true distribution of power often deviates from that intended in the design, and this deviation increases with frequency. FACET is a CAE tool which predicts the true power distribution. The author describes a graphical post-processing option in FACET which allows this distribution to be observed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Earth heterogeneity effects on the buried cable vulnerability to lightning
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The authors analyze the effect of the earth heterogeneity on the surges induced within buried cables by a nearby lightning discharge. A general formulation for the lightning induced electromagnetic fields in a multilayer Earth is developed in frequency domain by using a monopole technique. This technique is performed by the use of the so called modified transmission line model. Furthermore some numerical examples are given to illustrate the effect of the Earth structure on the severity of the impact of lightning on buried lines. This analysis is performed on the basis of the variation of the peak value of the electromagnetic fields induced along the cable outer conductor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of transmission line discontinuities for transient analysis in high speed systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The authors present methods to simulate transmission line discontinuities in the time-domain. The simulation procedures are distinguished by methods that describe discontinuities. To describe the behaviour of discontinuities, a quasi-static approach by lumped elements is used as well as a description by scattering parameters. The latter represents the general approach for the computation of discontinuity effects. The analysis by scattering parameters can be used for all discontinuities occurring in practice as for example mother board connectors. The methods are developed in such a way that they can easily be implemented in a transmission line simulator. Two examples are introduced, first a PCB-via connection, then a single transmission line with 90 degrees angles.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Technical rationale behind the proposed ANSI electrostatic discharge standard
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The American National Standards Institute (ANSI) is creating an ESD standard which provides guidance on electrostatic discharge testing procedures for electronic equipment using air discharge and contact discharge methodologies. The ANSI document contains material that has been ignored by other ESD standards and the authors who are ANSI committee members describe the issues which they feel should be covered by an ESD standard. Establishing ESD test criteria, evaluation of test results and furniture discharge simulation are described supported by experimental work.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Common mode current measurements and radiated emissions from long cable systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Given the size and complexity of the installations which are being measured, currently applied standards are of limited value in assessing their performance. Common mode current measurements for emissions offer an acceptable solution to an otherwise difficult problem. The degree of equivalence between the results quoted suggest that these alternative methods may prove the basis for a standard in their own right which will alleviate many of the problems associated with the measurements of large distributed systems. The experimental uncertainty estimates show that common mode current measurements are in excellent agreement with the CISPR 22 type radiated measurements. These measurements only consider emissions on the system cabling and do not consider direct board radiation. The author concludes that the most effective test procedure would include the measurement of both radiated field and conducted common mode signals when determining the compliance of a system containing large lengths of cable.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A mathematical model of concentrically loaded coaxial structures and its EMC applications
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Computer programs have been developed at Bristol University for modelling boxed microstrip lines. Modules from these programs have been modified and extended to produce a program which can model any uniform, symmetric, coaxial system that has multiple concentric dielectrics. The program has also been extended to model losses through the use of complex permeability and permittivity values for the dielectrics. The program can be used to find the distribution of fields and hence energy in the coaxial environment. It is a very useful research and development tool-for example it is hoped that it can be used to analyze the feasibility of making an absorbing device to reduce the common mode noise levels on cables coming out of equipment (a major source of electromagnetic noise).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Induced fast transients in multiconductor shielded cables
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The coupling of fast transient electromagnetic fields to lossy multiconductor shielded cables is considered. Calculation of the transient responses calls for the development of models simulating the cable, the incident field and the impressed sources. Accurate models are developed to simulate a multiconductor cable with a multilayer braided-shield and multiple parallel inner conductors or twisted-wire pairs. The incident field is the sum of the primary field, represented as a plane wave, and the wave reflected from the ground. The cable response is obtained in the frequency domain by means of an efficient matrix procedure, based on the transmission-line theory, which involves Thevenin-equivalent representation. The transient waveforms for any terminal load condition are computed by an inverse discrete Fourier transformation. The theoretical procedure is applied for evaluating transient voltages and currents induced by an EMP source on a bifilar twisted-wire line, with and without shield, above an aluminium or a ground plane.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The vehicle body as an electromagnetic shield-numerical simulation for emission and susceptibility studies
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: In understanding EMC in vehicles it is necessary to review briefly the external and internal environment. The external environment is either a test environment or an environment typical of road conditions. Examples of the former are EMC compliance tests in screened or anechoic rooms. The internal environment of the car can be described as a leaky metal cavity loaded with a variety of materials, e.g. engine parts, seating, driver, passengers etc. Numerical simulation techniques are the only approach capable of offering an overall picture of electromagnetic interactions in the complex car environment. A powerful numerical technique used for this purpose is described followed by some of the results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The implementation of the EMC Directive
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author sets the EMC Directive in its context in the new approach, describes the main features of the Directive and outlines some of the issues arising from its implementation in the UK.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A university postgraduate course in EMC
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: In preparation for the forthcoming EC legislation, UK electronics and electrical industries and industries whose products incorporate electrical or electronic elements will need a much higher level of expertise in electromagnetic compatibility than is currently available. The main objective of the MSc course described is to produce engineers whose knowledge of EMC will enable them to make important contributions to their companies up to and beyond 1992. It is anticipated that the demand for graduates from this course will be high, particularly via the part-time route. The course makes use of the existing screened room and the open-site facilities at the Universities of Hull and York.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Regulations standards and specifications relating to the implementation of the EMC Directive within the United Kingdom
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The authors examine the requirements necessary for compliance with the new approach EMC Directive No. 89/336/EEC. They describe the development of CEN/CENELEC standards and discuss generic standards, product specific EMC standards, transitional arrangements and the implications of the EMC directive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high field strength low-cost component susceptibility test facility
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: One method of determining the immunity to electromagnetic radiation of an electronic system is to subject it to a transverse electromagnetic (TEM) wave which is propagated between two parallel conductive plates. Techniques are described here which have been used to increase the maximum attainable field strength within such a parallel plateline, while using the same amplifier output power, and to reduce the effect of resonances which occurred in the screened room which enclosed the plateline.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC certification and accreditation programs in the US Navy
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The approach that was proposed by the US Navy has focused on the need for accreditation in two areas of EMC technical support, personnel providing direct technical support and laboratories doing MIL-STD-462 acceptance testing. Certification of personnel to a recognized and widely accepted standard would provide a basis for assuring that contractors and their Government counterparts were competent to provide technical advice on difficult issues. It would also provide a benchmark for Government use in training or replacing professional and technical staff. Accreditation of laboratories, both public and private, would help ensure that acceptance testing was performed according to a consistent standard. The responsibility for development of the EMC engineer and technician certification process was assigned to NAVAIR. NAVAIR issued an instruction establishing certification of engineers and technicians by the National Association of Radio and Telecommunications Engineers (NARTE), and accreditation of EMC test laboratories by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of the screening effectiveness of a large motor vehicle
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: A commercial vehicle was subjected to electromagnetic radiation, and the field within the cab was measured. Deductions were then made of the field anticipated at the point of measurement but without the vehicle present and thus the screening effectiveness could be determined. Observations were then made of the magnitude of any resonances which increased the in-cab strength. The commercial vehicle used for the test was of the type used for towing trailers to make an articulated combination. The tests were conducted in a semianechoic chamber which was 22 m by 10 m by 7 m high, and lined with 1.8 m absorbers. The electromagnetic field to which the vehicle was subjected was radiated from an antenna which was placed at five different positions around the vehicle. The field strength in the vehicle cab was measured by an isotropic field strength meter.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiated emission, susceptibility and crosstalk control on ground plane printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: In the case of conductors of finite width and with dielectrics of finite thickness it is shown that the closeness of the inductive coupling between conductor and ground plane is important in minimising the equivalent loop area at high frequencies. Alternating currents tend to follow a path which encloses the least magnetic flux, but in the case of a ground plane return it may be difficult to believe. An acceptance of this phenomenon is essential if certain advantages of ground planes are to be understood, therefore the results of a simple experiment which effectively demonstrates this are presented. As the current density under a conductor using the ground plane as a return has a direct influence on crosstalk, this effect can contribute a significant amount to crosstalk between conductors near ground plane boundaries. A method of plotting the mean current density over straight paths using simple probes which couple inductively into the plane was used to investigate this effect in a square board.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a system level bench test for the automotive industry
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author describes the experimental work carried out during the early stages of a project aimed at producing a system level bench test for automotive manufacturers and their suppliers. Susceptibility data on two vehicle systems obtained from bulk current injection tests is combined with transfer functions from open field trials and compared with results from radiated susceptibility chamber tests. Reasonable correlation is found between the susceptibilities predicted using BCI (bulk current injection) and those measured during radiated susceptibility chamber tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Distortion analysis of ultrafast pulses in interconnections on integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Transmission line theory is used to develop a model appropriate for interconnects in VLSI. Since ultimate device switching speeds can be no shorter than a few picoseconds, pulse lengths of 5 ps and 50 ps are studied. The case where both ground and signal lines are in the same metallisation layer of the process is studied and geometries appropriate for existing technologies are considered. A comparison of normal and superconducting metallisation is made to assess whether the inclusion of high temperature superconductors is a worthwhile proposition. The transmission matrix method based on ABCD parameters is used to take account of different physical properties or geometric changes along the length of a given line.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimization of topside electromagnetic environment (ships)
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The ship's topside electromagnetic environment is becoming more complex. The number of antennas has been increasing, radiation characteristics are becoming more varied, and there are more modes of operation and a larger library of radiating parameters. For the improvement of EMC characteristics on ships it is necessary to optimize the topside and the arrangement of antennas. The approach to optimization of the arrangement of antennas and topside design on ships based on the use of method of moments is proposed. Particular recommendations on the manual arrangement of antennas and topside design on ships by computer aided techniques and the results of measurements on ships have been extensively utilized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMP and transient suppressed mains filters
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: EMP protected mains filters currently being produced as standard products, provide various degrees of protection. Unfortunately, the precise degree of protection afforded is rarely defined clearly, and for a given filter range by a specific manufacturer, it can generally be deduced by the cost of the complete product. It is quite likely therefore, that when a particular range of EMP protected filters is more expensive than another, the difference in cost is often the key to the degree of protection provided. The author describes some tests which were undertaken to try and answer some of these questions, and attempts to put into perspective the different forms of EMP or transient suppressed mains filters which are generally available.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development of EMC measurement from GPO to Radio Agency
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author examines the history and technological advance of EMC measurement, with particular reference to the Post Office Radio Service and the evolution into the Radiocommunications Agency of the DTI. The topics covered include the use of early receiving equipment within the Radio Service and its subsequent development. Further discussion postulates on future trends as a direct result of technological developments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Co-ordination of IEC standards on EMC and the importance of participating in standards work
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author describes the coordination of EMC work that is being undertaken by the IEC, involving its own Technical Committees, specialized international organizations and, increasingly, CENELEC (European Committee for Electrotechnical Standardization).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple model of intermodulation spectra for use on a personal computer
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The authors describe initial work undertaken to characterise, from an EMC point of view, the RF environment in highly cluttered industrial site environments where a large number of radio systems may be present. The initial work involves bringing together existing methods and implementing these methods in an efficient manner on a personal computer. Further work involving calibration of the model against data from various measured environments is outlined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer aided design for radio-frequency interference reduction
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Describes the requirements for a computer aided design (CAD) package to predict radiated emissions from electronic equipment and to aid their reduction. Input for the package is obtained from a suite of CAD tools covering electrical and mechanical aspects of electronic equipment design. An electromagnetic solver using a method of moments technique is described and its current performance is indicated. The methods and problems of interfacing the package with the existing CAD packages are described, as are some of the challenges facing future users of integrated packages of this type.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aspects of the bulk current immunity test
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Susceptibility measurements pose extreme problems when the vehicle of interest is physically large as the case of aircraft. It is usually impractical to subject the equipment under test (EUT) to very high level electromagnetic fields in the open, in its operational mode. It is generally equally impractical to find a suitable enclosure within which well-conditioned high-level fields can be generated. A method currently being used to overcome this problem in the aircraft industry and elsewhere has been called bulk current injection. This involves injecting current into groups of cables entering ports of a selected part of the system being tested. This injection is carried out using a suitable form of magnetic coupling, between the signal source and the cable harnesses.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convenient current-injection immunity testing
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Describes a hand-held clamp-on current-injection tester intended for informal use. To minimise test time and to maximise the chances of finding susceptibility modes a wide range of frequencies and modulations is generated simultaneously. To ensure reproduceability current feedback from an independent transducer is provided.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMC implications of using unshielded twisted pair data busses in the aircraft environment
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Practical measurement data has been taken from the EMC tests carried out by BAe on a representative ARINC 629 Data Bus system using prototype hardware. The logical approach is given. The purpose of the tests was to establish the emission and susceptibility characteristics of the bus and its prototype interface hardware, and to compare these measured characteristics with the EMC specifications applicable to civil aircraft. These results are expected to be compared with similar work carried out by other organisations. The test categories covered were conducted and radiated emissions (CE&RE), induced signal susceptibility, and conducted and radiated susceptibility (CS&RS).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: First year graduate level course in electromagnetic combatibility
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Presents new ways for teaching such EMC topics as common and differential mode currents, shielding, and wire-to-wire/field-to-wire coupling methods. The objective is accomplished by first bringing 'the computer age' to the teaching of EMC/EMI. Some of the basic concepts of electromagnetic compatibility are covered by studying the approaches which several successful EMC modeling programs have used for solving the basic interference tasks. Finally the course directs the students to implement several of the learned modeling techniques into representative subsystems. A parallel objective of the course is to make analysis, rather than test, the most efficient way of implementing an EMC plan in the design stages of an electronic product.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A critical analysis of the immunity measurement methods for sound and television broadcast receivers
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: In order to protect the sound and video reception of broadcast programmes, the reduction of radiated and conducted disturbance from electric and electronic equipment, receivers included, is not sufficient. The characteristics of receiver immunity to ambient fields and conducted disturbances should also be very well considered. Emission measurements are not easy, but immunity measurements are more difficult, because the measuring circuit, and in particular the connection to the auxiliary equipment, can influence the results. Therefore the lay-out of the interconnecting cables should be well defined and the measurement methods standardized.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The Masterclass-teaching EMC in industry
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: To raise the awareness and technical ability of design engineers, Rolls-Royce and Associates (RRA) has started an in-house teaching programme to propagate the considerable experience existing within the Company. The lecture programme is based on this experience and the knowledge of senior engineers within the Company and is called the Masterclass. The author looks at the various technical needs of groups within the Company and the subsequent derivation of the EMC syllabus, to meet those needs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Preliminary investigations of coupling between twisted-wire-pairs
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Two methods of predicting frequency domain crosstalk in straight- and twisted-wire-pairs in the frequency range 300 kHz to 200 Mz are investigated. The method of Paul and McKnight (1979) is found to give much better quality predictions than that of Belevitch (1977).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simplified low-cost materials approach to shielding in EMC applications
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: With the advent of conductive polymers, it now appears feasible to take the basic concept of polymer concrete and make a conductive polymer concrete with tailored levels of electrical conductivity. In fact, preliminary conceptual studies point to the real possibility of arriving at a superconducting polymer concrete through the synergism achievable by the various components making up the composite. Collectively, Portland cement concrete and polymer concrete composites constitute two of the lowest cost but extremely versatile construction and industrial materials available in the world to-day. An intelligent but perhaps manoeuvred marriage of these materials can light the path to cheap & aesthetic shielding systems of interest in EMC applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of a missile body EMI gasket
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: A small missile body is being constructed from a series of interlocking sections made from aluminium alloys. Between each section an EMI gasket is fitted to ensure continuity of screening for the whole missile. The author describes how the electrical performance of this gasket has been determined both before and after exposure to a severe corrosive environment. A test method based on a measurement of gasket transfer impedance, using a triaxial test fixture, was developed. A significant factor was that the test jig was a full scale model of one of the joints between the sections, enabling precise design data to be obtained. The gasket used was of a novel design consisting of a conformable knitted circular monel metal mesh which is impregnated with a silicone gel. This silicone gel provided the environmental seal for the electrical contact points in the joint so preventing corrosion within the gasket area. This is essential to maintaining very low values of the joints transfer impedance to be maintained even after prolonged exposure to a severely corrosive environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effective lightning protection
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The author presents the lightning protection problems both in general terms and as a technical evaluation. He shows the importance of both the requirements of the protection units and their placing in a typical installation. A thorough understanding of lightning protection requirements is developed, removing the misconceptions that currently exist within the electrical industry regarding protection systems. He also reduces the lightning protection problems to an equivalent circuit, and then shows how this approach can be used to solve transient voltage problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of the US Navy's PC-based Frequency Assignment Computer Terminal System
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: In the past the US Navy's frequency records were kept either on microfiche or printed out on paper, and modifications and new assignments were penciled in on three-by five cards. This method of managing the spectrum became conspicuously archaic with the advent of computers that could perform EMC calculations and multiple frequency record transactions. To remedy this problem the US Navy, through the direction of the Chief of Naval Operations, established the PC-based Frequency Assignment Computer Terminal System (FACTS). As it was envisioned, FACTS was to provide an automated spectrum management capability to the multitude of Navy and Marine commands that have a daily responsibility of managing the use and allocation of the spectrum. Use of the FACTS has now spread to 102 users throughout the US Navy and is in operation in the Continental US, and in both the European and Pacific Theaters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EMP ship trial, planning, execution and result
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Electronic equipment fitted in naval vessels is extremely vulnerable to the effects of an electromagnetic pulse (EMP). The authors discuss briefly the theory of the generation of EMP, ship platform hardening techniques, conducting a ship EMP audit prior to an EMP trial, conducting an EMP ship trial, results obtained and concluding with the making of recommendations on how improvements can be made to the ship platform hardening.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement and testing method for large telecommunications systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Large telecommunication systems are assembled from independently operating sub-units and no two systems are identical. Each sub-unit has its own characteristic emission signature; these sub-units are coupled together with a multitude of differing cable types (screened and unscreened), and the whole system has an emission characteristic occupying a very wide frequency spectrum. Limitations within existing standards have been recognised and to cover the measurement of emissions from physically large telecommunication systems a draft standard has been developed. This draft has been accepted by European standards organisations as a proposed methodology for the testing of large telecommunication systems. Particular reference is made to the experience and preliminary results gained during the testing of a large telecommunications digital switching system on an open field site and measurements made in a shielded semianechoic chamber.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An experimental investigation into the performance of asymmetric screened rooms for electromagnetic measurements
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: An experimental investigation into the behaviour of asymmetric screened rooms is reported. A qualitative assessment of the theoretical basis is described as justification for the approach. Results are presented which illustrate the validity of the approach in suppressing field strength variations which can also be interpreted as mode control within the chambers. The results presented cover frequency scaled models corresponding to chambers of 50 wavelengths or so. It is shown that field strength deviation can be reduced to less than 10 dB over considerable frequency ranges. The work illustrates that by a simple modification of chamber wall shape a significant economic improvement can be made to chamber performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Prediction of PCB radiation in the presence of scattering bodies
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: Radiation from printed circuit boards (PCBs) is strongly influenced by the presence of other bodies. The aim of this work is to predict such interactions in a realistic environment, such as a piece of computing equipment, and provide a useful software tool for EMC design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An improved method for the performance evaluation of radiated emission test sites by a comb generator reference radiator
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: A fully automatic, computer-controlled site performance evaluation technique has been developed. This technique is capable of calibrating test sites for radiated emission testing of actual equipment. An important advantage of the technique is that calibrations are not limited to fields of dipole antennas, as in the concept of normalized site attenuation. The calibrations are carried out using field distributions which are equivalent to those generated by actual equipment under test. Thus, the new technique offers a significant improvement over previous methods, which utilize electric or spherical dipoles only.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation for electrostatic discharges
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The prime cause of breakdowns in electronic equipment today is still the effect of electrostatic discharges (ESD). The precise and reproducible simulation of such discharges using standardised and internationally recognised procedures is an indispensable tool for improving the quality of an electronic product by identifying potential weak spots during its development, production and/or installation. The requirements for reliable test rigs and the typical discharge waveforms obtained are discussed. Some details of today's highly specialised test equipment are given to show how closely the various simulation models emulate the conditions met in practice.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Testing civil aircraft and equipment to the new external RF environmental conditions
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The new certification requirements for civil aircraft to demonstrate that they can operate safely in high intensity radiated fields (HIRF) have had implications for both equipment and aircraft level EMC qualification susceptibility testing. At equipment level the Radio Technical Commission for Aeronautics (RTCA) has been revising the environmental specification D0160B which covers all environmental testing including EMC. At aircraft level both EUROCAE and the Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE) have been involved in the production of an Advisory Circular detailing the requirements and defining the environment and a Users Guide covering design, analysis and test methods for showing the aircraft is compliant with the requirements. The paper outlines the current requirements and discusses the test procedure that can be used to demonstrate compliance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Instrumentation configurations for the performance of EMP test procedures
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Electromagnetic Compatibility, 1990
abstract: The authors briefly review the details associated with EMP hardness test procedures in MIL-STD-188-125 (draft) and MIL-STD-461C/462. These tests are important to nuclear weapon effects engineers because they simulate the stress of an electromagnetic pulse which a military electronics system will experience. Included are details of the equipment configurations for the tests, a discussion of the areas where caution should be exercised in order to obtain valid results, and descriptions of lessons learned during the conduct of actual test programs. The radiated susceptibility procedures of MIL-STD-461C/462 simulate the EMP threat to the entire system or subsystem and the conducted susceptibility procedures inject transient pulses on the wires and cables. The test methods of MIL-STD-188-125 (draft) address HEMP hardness testing of ground based Command, Control, Communication, Computer and Intelligence (C/sup 4/I) facilities. These published EMP standard procedures are used to develop acceptance and verification test plans tailored to stress the equipment under test in a configuration which is close to that found on the battlefield.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
